newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila rail says drops Credit Suisse as financier.
newsitem.headline: Manila rail says drops Credit Suisse as financier.

text.p: Credit Suisse of Switzerland had been dropped from the list of financiers for the EDSA Metro-Rail Transit, to be built in Manila at a cost of nearly $750 million, the railway builders said on Thursday.

Robert Sobrepena, chairman of Fil-Estate Land Inc, which heads the consortium building the railway, told reporters that Credit Suisse would not join the financial closing for the project in August as Japanese banks had offered a better deal.
Sobrepena said creditors led by the Bank of Tokyo and the Japan Export-Import Bank took a very aggressive stance and gave better terms.
EDSA MRT, comprising seven Filipino companies, needs loans of at least $550 million. Members of the consortium have already contributed $190 million in equity.
Sobrepena said the Japanese banks had offered much lower interest rates for the loans as well as guarantees.
The Japanese banks were invited by the MRT's contractors, Sumitomo Corp and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, he said.

The MRT, a 16.8-kilometre (10.4-mile) railway connecting one business district in the city to the main thoroughfare, is to be built under a 25-year Build-Lease-Transfer agreement between the consortium and the Department of Transport and Communications.
